packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-10 - unverified image-only reading
Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. Blind reading. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (opened only the brief, PROMPT.md and image files in this packet; I opened image files by guessed sequential names since listing the directory was not permitted).

LAYOUT SURVEY (from image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- Single small paper(?) or parchment slip, landscape, photographed on black with a colour checker and cm ruler (roughly 15 x 10.5 cm visible from ruler).
- Long-line text, one column, no ruling visible. About 9 lines of text in a single cursive/humanistic-cursive hand, darker ink, written across the full width; right edge appears to cut off line ends (lines 2, 6, 9 run to the edge).
- Line 1 (top): an alphabet sequence "A a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r s t v ..." in lighter/browner ink, beginning with a larger "A"; it runs off the right edge.
- Lines 2-9: short sentences, each beginning with an enlarged initial (M, P, P, P, P, C, Q?) - look like schoolroom/exercise phrases ("Praeceptor liceat mihi ...") rather than a book text. Observation only.
- Bottom (line 10): another alphabet start "A a b c d e f g h i k l ..." in pale ink, partly cut at the bottom edge.
- Left margin: a later note written vertically (rotated 90 degrees), reading upward, apparently a modern/archival note with a date-like "15(?)35" - see below.
- Lower right: a modern pencil shelfmark-style note (not part of the text).
- No rubrics, no glosses, no columns. Edges: right edge cuts line ends; bottom edge cuts the final alphabet line.

TRANSCRIPTION
Line numbers are counted from the top of each image (text lines only). Tiles overlap; overlaps noted.

image-002.jpg (native tile, top-left of slip; shows left ~40% of lines 1-5, top of line 6)
002-1  A ·ab c d e f g h i[...]        (alphabet, browner ink; large A preceded by a short horizontal stroke; a point before "a")
002-2  Manus meae Speciuneu(?) exh[...]   (large calligraphic M; the third word is written "Sp" + "ecimen"-like letters, read as "Specimen"? with a final stroke that may be "u"/"n"; long descender on S)
002-3  Praeceptor liceat mihi exir[...]
002-4  Praeceptor liceat mihi exire[...]
002-5  Praeceptor liceat mihi exire[...]
002-6  [top of a capital P, rest cut by tile edge]
   Note: "Praeceptor" written "Praeceptor" with ae ligature/ae spelled out ("Praeceptor" letters P-r-a-e-c-e-p-t-o-r); initial P's are large looped capitals, the loops of lines 3-5 joined in the left margin.
Left margin (rotated 90 degrees, reading bottom-to-top, pencil, modern hand, not part of text): "Einband(?) [..]" then "II/6" with a stroke, then "33 (Ausg...?" - continues on another tile.

image-003.jpg (native tile, top-right; overlaps 002 at "f g h" in line 1; shows right part of lines 1-5, line 5 partly cut at bottom)
003-1  [...]f g h i k l m n o p q r ꝛ ſ s t v u    (alphabet continued: long-s and round s both given; "r" followed by r-rotunda/2-shaped r; a point after "p"(?) is an ink blot; last letter(s) at the right edge partly cut, a further letter below the line at the edge, possibly "u"/"w")
003-2  [...]imen exhibeo praeceptor · mundas a uicius(?)   (overlap: "...imen" continues 002-2 "Speci..."; last word "uicius"/"uirius"? - minims ambiguous; I do not settle it)
003-3  [...]mihi exire ad purgandu(m) [?]ctum ·    (between "purga" and "ndu" the letters look like "purgaundu"; then a darker, apparently re-inked group "ctum"/"ctrum"? with a long horizontal stroke above "ndu..." running right - possibly an abbreviation stroke or a correction; reading of last word uncertain; point at end)
003-4  [...]mihi exirere(?) ad reddenda(m) urina(m)   ("exirere"/"exiuere": letters look like e-x-i-r-e-r-e, maybe a slip for "exire"; "reddendā" with overline on final a; "urina" with a curl/stroke above, perhaps abbreviation for final m)
003-5  [...]mihi exire ut adferam carta(m)· Prima[...]   ("cartā"? overline over final a; after the point a word beginning "Pr" or "Pri", cut at bottom of tile; see overview: "Primas(?) a[...]")

image-004.jpg (native tile, bottom-left; top line overlaps 002-5/line 4 descender; shows left part of lines 5-10)
004-1  [descenders/feet of line 4: "...liceat exir..." cut at top]  (overlap with 002-4)
004-2  Praeceptor liceat mihi exir[...]      (= 002-5, overlap)
004-3  Pulsatu(m) est : u?saur(?) si libet q[...]   ("Pulsatū" with stroke over u; colon-like double point after "est"; next word has an i/stroke above, letters u-s/h-a-u-r or "ue?sau"; I cannot settle it - perhaps an abbreviated word; then long-s "si libet")
004-4  Campana mo ad alia vel d[...]   ("Campana" with large C; "mo"/"uo"? short word, maybe abbreviated; "ad alia"; "vel" written "uel" with abbreviation-like ascender; then "d" of next word)
004-5  Quaera(?) si libet Diaconu(m)[...]   (large looped Q; following letters "uaara"/"uaera" with a long stroke above - possibly an abbreviated word "Quaera" / "Quaerere"?; "si libet"; "Diaconu" + minims, cut at tile edge)
004-6  A a b c d e f g h i l l[...]   (bottom alphabet, pale ink, lower halves cut by the bottom edge of the slip)
Left margin (pencil, rotated, reading bottom-to-top): "(...) 33 (Ausg? ) | 1525(?) / 1535(?))" - last group reads "(1535)" or "(1525)" ending in ")" - modern archival note, not text.

image-005.jpg (native tile, bottom-right; overlaps 003-4/003-5 at top and 004 on the left; shows right part of lines 4-9)
005-1  [...]liceat exirere(?) ad reddenda(m) urina   (= 003-4, overlap; final word has no visible abbreviation stroke here except a small curl above at the end, seen in 003)
005-2  [...]mihi exire ut adferam carta(m)(?)· P(er)nas(?) atra[...]   (overlap with 003-5; "cartā" with stroke over the last a; after the point: "P" with a stroke through/attached descender + "nas" or "rnas", read "Pennas?"/"Prnas?" - unresolved; then "atra" cut by the right edge)
005-3  [...]? si libet quid actu(m)(?) oportet ·   (continues 004-3 "Pulsatum est : ... si libet q-"; "actū" with a superscript stroke/i-like mark above the final letter; "oportet" with point after)
005-4  [...]alia vel domestica quarta u?erat(?) ·   (continues 004-4 "Campana mo ad alia vel d-"; "domestica" letters d-o-m-e-s(long)-t-i-c-a; last word "uerat"/"ucat"/"nerat" with an overline above - abbreviated, perhaps "vocat"? unresolved; point at end)
005-5  [...]Diaconu(m)· Prioratu(m)?· prouincialem· vel[...]   (continues 004-5 "Quaera si libet Diaconu-"; "Diaconū"; second word "Prioraū"/"Prioratu" with stroke over the end; third word "pro/p(ro)uincialem" with p bearing a crossed descender, letters "puinciale" + minims; "vel" at the right edge, rest cut off)
005-6  [stray strokes of the bottom alphabet line at left; rest blank to the edge]
Modern pencil note lower right (not text): "Stams, STA, Frg. 38K" (my reading). This is a holding/shelfmark label visible in the image; it does not identify the work.

SUMMARY OF CONNECTED TEXT (lines of the slip; each line assembled from overlapping tiles; uncertain readings marked)
L1  A ·a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r ꝛ ſ s t v u[...]
L2  Manus meae Speci(m)en(?) exhibeo praeceptor · mundas a uicius(?)
L3  Praeceptor liceat mihi exire ad purgandu(m) [?]ctum(?) ·
L4  Praeceptor liceat mihi exirere(?) ad reddenda(m) urina(m)
L5  Praeceptor liceat mihi exire ut adferam carta(m) · P?nas(?) atra[...]
L6  Pulsatu(m) est : u?saur(?) si libet quid actu(m)(?) oportet ·
L7  Campana mo(?) ad alia vel domestica quarta u?erat(?) ·
L8  Quaera(?) si libet Diaconu(m) · Prioratu(m)(?) · prouincialem · vel[...]
L9  A a b c d e f g h i l l[...]   (pale, cut at bottom)

LIMITATIONS
- All text on the slip was covered by the four tiles; nothing on this face remains unread, but the right edge cuts the ends of L1, L5 and L8, and the bottom edge cuts L9.
- Unresolved words: L2 last word; L3 last word (darker re-inked letters, possible correction); L4 "exirere"; L5 word after the point; L6 word after "est :"; L7 "mo" and last word; L8 first word and "Prioratu".
- The above covers face 1 only (image-001 overview + tiles 002-005). Correction: image-006 turned out to be a second overview, of the other face; see below.

FACE 2 - LAYOUT SURVEY (image-006.jpg, reduced overview)
- Same slip, other face, held flat by two clear weights. Landscape, long lines, no ruling visible.
- Top: 7 lines in a smaller, denser cursive in dark ink, written edge to edge (line ends cut at the right edge). Content visibly repeats face 1 as running text with slashes "/" separating the phrases: "Pulsatum est ... si libet quid actum oportet / campana ... ad a[lia] / domestica ... vocat(?) / ... si libet diaconum prior..." then two alphabet lines ("A a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r ꝛ s t v u w x y z ..."), then "Manus meae specimen exhibeo preceptor ... / preceptor liceat mihi exire ad purgandum aluu(m)(?) / preceptor liceat mihi exire ad ... / ...urinam(?)". Observation of word shapes at overview scale only; tiles will be read for the text.
- An interlinear addition "ad" appears above line 2 (above "quedam"?).
- Middle: blank; modern pencil label at left "Stams, STA, Frg. 38V"(?).
- Bottom: two lines written upside down relative to the top block (i.e. the same orientation as face 1 rotated 180°?): "Praeceptor liceat mihi" (short line) and "Manus meae specimen exhibeo praeceptor · mundas a vitiis(?)"-type line, in larger hand, plus a large M with flourish. Reading these will need the tile rotated mentally.
- Bottom edge: stains and a small hole near centre.

FACE 2 TRANSCRIPTION
image-007.jpg (native tile, top-left of face 2; shows left ~half of top block lines 1-7, and pencil label)
Hand: smaller, more angular cursive than face 1, long ascenders with forked tops, many long descending strokes; possibly a different writer or the same writer writing faster. Faint long vertical pen strokes (trials?) cross lines 1-7.
007-1  Pulsatum est u?sau(?) si libet quit[...]   ("Pulsatum" with superscript stroke/u over the u; the word after "est" again u/n-s-a-u- with a final i/minim and a flourish; same unresolved word as face-1 L6; "quit" for quid)
007-2  domestica q?uedam(?) u nocat(?) / Q?ua[...]   (interlinear "ad" written above the second word; second word "quedam"/"quadam"? - letters q-u-e-d-a-m with a looped first letter; then a single "u" and "nocat"/"uocat" with a point/mark above; slash; then a looped capital (Q or O) + "ua..." cut by the tile edge)
007-3  [...]uincialem vel aliu(m) A a b c d e f g[...]   (starts mid-word "uincialem" - i.e. this line continues a word broken from line 2; "vel" written "uel"; "aliu" with superscript u/stroke; then an alphabet begins with a decorated A)
007-4  A a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r ꝛ[...]   (second alphabet, large flourished A at line start)
007-5  Manus meae specimen exhibeo p[...]   (large M with pen flourishes above, intruding into line 4; "specimen" here clearly s-p-e-c-i-m-e-n with long s; "exhibeo" with h)
007-6  mihi exire ad purgandum aluu(m)(?)[...]   ("aluu" with superscript u-mark; read "aluum"? - unresolved; an "ad" small above "exire"? no - a loop above "purgandum" from line 5's descender)
007-7  urina(m)(?) ꝫ(?)   (word "urina" + minims; ends with a long-s-like or "ꝫ"-like sign; ascenders cut by ruling? - uncertain)
Pencil label lower left (modern, not text): "Stams, STA, Frg. 38V".

image-008.jpg (native tile, top-right of face 2; overlaps 007 by a few words; lines 1-6 of top block; line 7 does not extend this far)
008-1  [...]libet quit actu(m)(?) oportet / campana me(?) ad a[...]   (overlap "libet quit" with 007-1; "actū"/"actui" with superscript mark as on face 1; "oportet"; slash; "campana" with long first stroke; "me"/"mo"? two letters; "ad a" at the right edge, cut)
008-2  [...]at / Q?suaream(?) si libet diaconum priorem(?)[...]   (overlap "-at /" = 007-2 "nocat /"; first word: looped capital (Q/O) then "suaream"/"suaream" - unresolved, I do not normalise it; "diaconum" with superscript mark; "priorem" or "prioren" cut at edge, a small "ↄ"-like mark above the line near here)
008-3  [...]A a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r ꝛ ſ s t o? u v w x y z ꝫ   (overlap with 007-3 alphabet start; ends with z and a flourished ꝫ-like sign; some letters doubled/variant forms - u/v, two s-forms)
008-4  [...]o p q r ꝛ ſ s t v u w x y z ꝫ ·   (continuation of the second alphabet from 007-4; similar ending with flourish and dots)
008-5  [...]exhibeo preceptor mund?es(?) a uicys(?) / precep[...]   ("preceptor" spelled with e, unlike face 1; next word m/w-e-n-d-e-s or "mundes"; "a"; last word "uicys"/"uicijs"/"ueyse"? with a mark above - unresolved; slash; "precep-" cut at edge)
008-6  [...]um aluu(m) / preceptor liceat mihi exire ad[...]   ("aluu" with superscript u-like sign as in 007-6; slash; "preceptor liceat mihi exire ad", "ad" at edge with dots)
Below line 6: blank paper with stains; long faint vertical pen strokes from above.

image-009.jpg (native tile, bottom-left of face 2; overlaps 007 at the pencil label)
- Mostly blank; pencil label "Stams, STA, Frg. 38V" (= 007, overlap).
009-1 (near bottom, written upside down relative to the top block; read by rotating 180°):  [...]eptor : mundis(?) a uicijs(?)   (pale brown ink, larger hand like face 1; "[praec]eptor" cut at the right of the tile; colon; "mundis"/"mundes"; "a"; last word "uicijs"/"uitijs"? with i-dots - unresolved)
- Along the very bottom edge: rust-brown fragmentary letter shapes, cut by the edge (e.g. a "3"/z-like form in a damaged box near centre), apparently remains of a further line of writing trimmed off, or offset/stain; not readable as words.

image-010.jpg (native tile, bottom-right of face 2; overlaps 009 at the damaged box near the bottom edge)
Two lines upside down relative to the top block. Read with the image rotated 180°; numbered in rotated reading order (first = nearest the bottom edge of the image):
010-a  Manus meae Specimen exhibeo Praeceptor : mu[...]   (large M with three parallel flourish strokes; "Specimen" with long S; "Praeceptor" with ae; colon; continues on 009-1 as "...mundis(?) a uicijs(?)" - the "eptor : mu" overlap joins the two tiles)
010-b  Praeceptor liceat mihi   (large P with a round loop; "Praeceptor" abbreviated-looking "Praecep" + "tor"; then "liceat mihi"; line stops after "mihi" - unfinished)
Same pale-brown ink and larger hand as face 1 lines 2-8; these two lines duplicate the opening of face 1 (L2-L3). Bottom edge: same rust-brown cut letter remains as in 009 (e.g. "3"/z shapes), unreadable.

FACE 2 SUMMARY (top block, dense hand, joined across 007/008; uncertain readings marked)
T1  Pulsatum est u?sau(?) si libet quit actu(m)(?) oportet / campana me(?) ad a[...]
T2  domestica q?uedam(?) [interlinear: ad] u nocat(?) / Q?suaream(?) si libet diaconum priorem(?)[...]
T3  [pro]uincialem vel aliu(m) A a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r ꝛ ſ s t o? u v w x y z ꝫ
T4  A a b c d e f g h i k l m n o p q r ꝛ ſ s t v u w x y z ꝫ ·
T5  Manus meae specimen exhibeo preceptor mund?es(?) a uicys(?) / precep[tor ...]
T6  mihi exire ad purgandum aluu(m)(?) / preceptor liceat mihi exire ad[...]
T7  urina(m)(?) ꝫ(?)
Bottom (inverted): "Manus meae Specimen exhibeo Praeceptor : mundis(?) a uicijs(?)" / "Praeceptor liceat mihi".

OVERALL LIMITATIONS AND NOTES
- Both faces read across all supplied tiles (image-001..010; 001 and 006 are overviews). No image-limit removal occurred.
- Observation: the slip contains alphabet rows and short repeated Latin phrases addressed to a "praeceptor", written twice (face 1 large hand, face 2 dense hand + an inverted start); this looks like writing exercises. That is an interpretation, not an identification.
- Right edges of face 2 top block lines are cut; T2/T3 show a word broken across lines ("prior..." / "...uincialem"), so the cut loses little at that point, but T1 "ad a[...]" and T5 "precep[...]" lose text.
- Unresolved words recurring on both faces: the word after "Pulsatum est" (u/n-s-a-u-r/i), the word after "domestica" (face 1 "quarta", face 2 "quedam"? with "ad" above), the last word of the "domestica" phrase (face 1 "uerat"?, face 2 "u nocat"?), the first word of the "si libet diaconum" phrase (face 1 "Quaera"?, face 2 "Q?suaream"), and "mundas/mundes/mundis a uicius/uicys/uicijs". Face 2 T6 "aluum(?)" may bear on face-1 L3's last word "[?]ctum", which I read independently and left unresolved.
- Visible pencil labels name a holding ("Stams, STA, Frg. 38R/38V" as I read them; first was read "38K" but is probably R). These are shelfmark labels on the images, not identifications of the work.
